H-02.title: No `unwrap`/`expect`/`unwrap_unchecked`/`unwrap_err`/`expect_err` in production code, including doctest examples.

H-04.title: No panicking index or slice on data whose bounds are not proven by construction.

H-07.title: No `Box::leak`, `mem::forget`, `transmute`, `static mut`, or `'static` added to silence lifetimes.

H-08.title: No clones to appease the borrow checker.

H-09.title: No `String`, `Box<dyn Error>` or `anyhow`/`eyre` errors in public library signatures.

H-10.title: No silently discarded failures (`let _ =`, `.ok();`, empty `Err` arms, masking defaults).

H-11.title: No lossy `as` numeric casts, including enum discriminants: map a fieldless enum to a code with an exhaustive `match` in `From`.

H-12.title: Never weaken verification (tests, lints, hooks, CI) to get green.

H-13.title: Bounded resources: channels, buffers, timeouts, owned tasks and threads (joined or aborted; `spawn_blocking` tasks awaited).

OWN-01.title: Borrow in parameters, own in returns.

OWN-02.title: Take ownership when the callee stores or transforms the value.

OWN-04.title: Choose the receiver deliberately: `&self` to query, `&mut self` to mutate, `self` to convert, consume or transition typestate.

OWN-06.title: Borrowing structs (`struct View<'a>`) are for short-lived views, parsers and iterators.

OWN-07.title: Do not add `'static` bounds, `Box::leak` or globals to silence lifetime errors.

OWN-08.title: Resolve borrow conflicts by restructuring, not cloning.

OWN-09.title: Use the entry API for insert-or-update.

OWN-10.title: Return `Cow<'_, T>` when a function usually borrows but sometimes must allocate.

OWN-12.title: Interior mutability (`Cell`, `RefCell`, `Mutex`, atomics) is a documented design decision on the type.

OWN-13.title: Return iterators or slices instead of allocating a collection the caller only iterates.

OWN-15.title: Use `Box<str>`, `Box<[T]>`, `Arc<str>` or `Arc<[T]>` for immutable owned data that never grows.

OWN-16.title: Derive `Copy` only for small value-like types that will stay small.

OWN-17.title: Return results by value, as a tuple or named struct when there are several.

API-11.title: Mark values that must be used `#[must_use]`: pure constructors, builders, iterators and computed results.

API-12.title: Seal traits that are not meant to be implemented downstream, and say so in the trait's docs.

API-18.title: Traits are small, cohesive role interfaces.

API-19.title: Do not implement `Deref` to emulate inheritance.

API-20.title: Use `#[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]` on public traits users are likely to misimplement.

API-21.title: Generic `struct` and `enum` definitions carry no trait bounds; put them on the `impl` blocks that need them.

ERR-02.title: Scope error types to an operation or module, with a closed set of variants callers can act on.

ERR-03.title: Variants carry diagnostic context (path, id, offending value) as typed fields, not preformatted strings.

ERR-05.title: Error messages are lowercase, have no trailing punctuation, and describe this layer's failure.

ARC-01.title: Use a workspace with a virtual manifest and members under `crates/`.

ARC-02.title: Dependencies point inward: domain (pure) before application (use cases, ports) before adapters (I/O) before binaries (composition root).

ARC-03.title: Ports are traits owned by the consumer (the application layer) and implemented by adapters.

ARC-05.title: One concept per module, with a small surface.

ARC-11.title: Parse configuration once at startup into validated typed structs and pass it down.

ARC-12.title: Justify every dependency (maintenance, size, license, `cargo deny`).

ARC-14.title: Binaries are thin: parse input, build the object graph (composition root), run, and map errors to exit codes.

ARC-15.title: Write a macro only when functions, generics or traits cannot express the idea.

TST-02.title: Test through the narrowest real seam.

TST-04.title: Tests return `Result` and use `?` for setup.

TST-05.title: Assert exact values and exact error variants.

TST-06.title: Use property tests (`proptest`) for invariants, round-trips and algebraic laws in parsers, codecs and domain rules.

TST-07.title: Use snapshot tests (`insta`) for structured or textual output, and review snapshots as code.

TST-08.title: Prove type-level guarantees (typestate, sealing, deliberate `!Send`) with compile-fail tests (`trybuild` or `compile_fail` doctests).

TST-09.title: Test doubles are hand-written fakes of port traits.

TST-10.title: Tests are deterministic: no sleeps, no wall clock, no real network, no shared global state, no order dependence.

TST-11.title: Public entry points have runnable doctests that use `?`, not `unwrap`.

TST-14.title: Build test data with builder or fixture functions.

TST-15.title: Keep feedback fast: use `cargo nextest` when available, keep unit tests in milliseconds, and isolate slow tests.

TST-16.title: Every performance claim ships with a benchmark (`criterion` or `divan`).

PERF-03.title: Prefer iterators and adapters (`extend`, `retain`, `drain`, `windows`, `as_chunks::<N>()`) to index loops.

PERF-05.title: Keep hot types small: at or below 128 bytes on 64-bit targets, pinned with a `const` size assertion that holds on every target.

PERF-08.title: Hot generic code uses static dispatch.

PERF-09.title: Keep the template's release, profiling, bench and dev profiles.

PERF-10.title: Bound everything that grows with input: sizes, collections, recursion depth, concurrency (`Semaphore`), queue lengths (H-13).

PERF-12.title: Keep critical sections short: drop every guard before I/O, sleeps, joins, blocking channel operations or calls into unknown code.

ASY-01.title: Use async only for I/O-bound concurrency.

ASY-03.title: Use native `async fn` in traits, not `#[async_trait]`.

ASY-06.title: Never block in async code: no `std::thread::sleep`, blocking I/O, or heavy CPU, and no lock guard across `.await` (H-14).

ASY-08.title: Put timeouts on all external I/O.

ASY-09.title: Share state by message passing (an actor owns it) before reaching for `Arc<Mutex<_>>`.

ASY-10.title: For sync parallelism use `std::thread::scope` (borrowing) or `rayon` (data parallel).

ASY-11.title: Keep public types, and the futures public `async fn`s return, `Send` (types also `Sync`), and assert it at compile time.

ASY-12.title: Use async closures (`async |x| ...`, `AsyncFn*` bounds) for borrowed, non-spawned callbacks.

ASY-13.title: Every atomic ordering is justified in a comment: `Relaxed` says why no other memory depends on the value, `Acquire`/`Release`/`AcqRel` name…

ASY-15.title: Spawn threads with `thread::Builder` (`spawn`, `spawn_scoped`), named, and propagate the `io::Error`: `thread::spawn` and `Scope::spawn` pa…

ASY-17.title: Do not build synchronization primitives (locks, once-cells, semaphores, channels) from atomics.

OUT-01.title: Wire types (DTOs) are separate from domain types when the external shape differs or must version independently.

OUT-02.title: Public contracts pin serde conventions: `rename_all` at the type level, explicit enum tagging, `deny_unknown_fields` on inbound commands an…

OUT-03.title: Persisted and public schemas carry a version.

OUT-04.title: Output is deterministic: stable field order, `BTreeMap` for maps, sorted collections, and injected time and ids.

OUT-06.title: CLIs offer a machine mode (`--format json`): data to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, meaningful `ExitCode`s, and JSON Lines for streams.

OUT-07.title: Generate JSON Schemas for public contracts with `schemars` and snapshot them to catch breaking changes.

OUT-08.title: Log with `tracing`: structured fields, spans (`#[instrument(skip_all, fields(...))]`), no `println!` in libraries, and no secrets or PII.

OUT-09.title: Use zero-copy deserialization (`&'de str`, `Cow<'de, str>`, `#[serde(borrow)]`) for large or hot inputs.

OUT-10.title: `Display` is for users and `Debug` is for developers.

MOD-02.title: Use `let ... else` for early exits, `if let` chains instead of nested `if let`, and `if let` guards in match arms (1.95+).

MOD-04.title: Use native `async fn` in traits and async closures, not `async-trait` or boxed-closure workarounds.

MOD-05.title: Use `#[expect(lint, reason = "...")]`, never `#[allow]`, and only under H-05.

MOD-06.title: Know the 2024 capture rules: return-position `impl Trait` captures all in-scope lifetimes.

MOD-07.title: Prefer modern std APIs to hand-rolled equivalents: `is_some_and`, `is_none_or`, `inspect_err`, `take_if`, `repeat_n`, `chunk_by`, `as_chunk…

MOD-08.title: Use `core::error::Error` for `no_std`-compatible libraries, and `std::fmt::from_fn` for one-off `Display` adapters.

MOD-10.title: Use const generics, `const fn` and inline `const { }` where compile-time evaluation clarifies intent.

MOD-11.title: Use trait upcasting (`&dyn Sub` to `&dyn Super`), not `as_any` hacks.

MOD-12.title: Use `cfg_select!` (1.95+) instead of the `cfg-if` crate in new code.

MOD-13.title: In CI, set `build.warnings = "deny"` (Cargo 1.97+) rather than `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`, which invalidates the build cache.

CRF-01.title: Names reveal intent in the domain's own language.

CRF-02.title: A function does one thing at one level of abstraction.

CRF-04.title: Comments explain why, doc comments explain the contract, there is no commented-out code, and `TODO(#issue)` carries a reference.

CRF-05.title: No dead code, unused dependencies (`cargo machete`), unused features or speculative generality: no single-implementation trait that is not…

CRF-06.title: Format with `rustfmt` using the repository config; its output is authoritative.

CRF-08.title: Leave the code cleaner within the change's scope.

CRF-09.title: Replace magic numbers with named constants or unit-bearing types (`Duration`, newtypes).

CRF-10.title: Write expression-oriented code (`let x = match ...`) and iterator pipelines when they read more clearly than loops, but do not code-golf.

CRF-11.title: Rustdoc and READMEs describe the current contract and behaviour.

PROC-01.title: Explore before editing: crate charter, public API, tests, call sites.

PROC-02.title: Delegate wide searches to an exploration subagent and keep conclusions only.

PROC-03.title: Plan non-trivial changes: goal, invariants, signatures, placement, errors, test list, risks, HITL decisions.

PROC-05.title: Take small steps: one behavior per red-green-refactor cycle, build and test each step, and commit when green if commits are in scope.

PROC-06.title: For multi-step work, keep the plan file's checklist current so compaction or handoff loses nothing.

PROC-07.title: Self-review the diff against the checklist before requesting review, and fix what you find.

PROC-08.title: Every change that reaches "done" gets an independent fresh-context review.

PROC-09.title: After two failed attempts at the same compiler error, stop and re-model ownership before trying again.

PROC-12.title: Read the whole diagnostic, including notes, help and `rustc --explain`, before changing code.
